description: Connection interrupted measures commands, not time: shown when the usercmd made 127 commands ago is newer than the last one the server acknowledged (nextSnap->ps.commandTime). One command per client frame makes the warning window 127 frames: about 1 s at 125 FPS, 254 ms at 500, 127 ms at 1000, so high frame rates show it on healthy connections. While the player is not simulating (kill cam, final kill cam) commandTime stops advancing and the window drains even faster.
evidence: CG_DrawDisconnect: CL_GetUserCmd(CL_GetCurrentCmdNumber() - 0x7F); shown if nextSnap->ps.commandTime < cmd.serverTime <= cg.time. CL_CreateNewCommands (004EF7A0): cmdNumber++ into a 128-entry ring (& 0x7F). Store build: CG_DrawDisconnect 1400DA680, CL_CreateNewCommands 1401954D0 (match.py). To confirm in reconstruction: CL_SendCmd (004EC0A0) creates one command per frame, and whether the wrapped ring also costs real command redundancy in CL_WritePacket (004FCB30). Players report it clears when capped at 120 FPS.

description: The game changes Windows microphone settings: Voice_Init sets the record level of every wave-in mixer line to winvoice_mic_reclevel (default 0xFFFF, i.e. 100%) and their mute state to winvoice_mic_mute, and Voice_Playback re-applies the level whenever the dvar changes. Mixer_RestoreWaveInRecordLevels puts them back only on a clean shutdown, so a crash or forced exit leaves the system microphone at 100%. A game has no business changing system device settings; scale the captured samples in the game instead (winvoice_mic_scaler already exists).
evidence: Voice_Init (0079EBD0): Mixer_SetWaveInRecordLevels(Dvar_GetInt(winvoice_mic_reclevel)), Mixer_SetWaveInMuteStates(winvoice_mic_mute). Mixer_SetWaveInRecordLevels: mixerGetLineControlsA(MIXERCONTROL_CONTROLTYPE_VOLUME 0x50030001) then mixerSetControlDetails. Store build imports the same WINMM mixer functions; Voice_Init matched at 14049E3B0.

description: Removes a key with strcpy(start, s) where the two overlap (the rest of the string copied down over the key). Undefined behaviour that works because VC100 expands strcpy into a forward byte copy; Info_RemoveKey_Big (0078ECD0) does the same.
evidence: Disassembly at 0078EC8D: an inline byte loop from s down to start. src/universal/q_shared.cpp reproduces it with tools/recon/include/string.h's forward-copy strcpy.

description: Off by one: the append is refused only when strlen(newi) + strlen(s) > MAX_INFO_STRING (1024), so the string can grow to 1024 characters plus its terminator, one byte past a MAX_INFO_STRING buffer. Info_SetValueForKey_Big (0078F1E0) has the same check against BIG_INFO_STRING. Quake III refuses at >=.
evidence: Disassembly at 0078F140: CMP EDX,0x400; JBE (append). Reachable from the network wherever a caller's string or value comes from a client or server (userinfo); the callers aren't reviewed yet.

description: Stack overflow: a big info string may be up to BIG_INFO_STRING (20480) characters, but each key is copied into an 8192-byte stack buffer with no length check, so a key longer than 8191 characters overwrites the stack. (The value is only skipped: the original's value copy was compiled out.)
evidence: Disassembly at 0078ED31: the key loop writes into [EBP-0x2004] (pkey) until a backslash, with no bound; the only length check is on the whole string (0078ECFD: CMP EAX,0x5000). Whether a caller passes network data isn't reviewed yet.

description: Not the inverse of GetLeanFraction (2f - f*f): any fraction below 1 is first lowered by 0.8, so 0.9 maps to 0.0513 where the inverse is 0.684, and everything up to 0.8 maps to 0.
evidence: Disassembly at 0078FD3E: SUBSS by 0.8 (0x00B95868) when fFrac < 1, then 1 - sqrt(1 - fFrac). Callers (lean prediction) not checked: may be deliberate.

description: Copies the path through a 64-byte buffer before appending the extension, silently cutting any path of 64 characters or more; an empty path reads path[-1].
evidence: Disassembly at 00790308: I_strncpyz(oldPath, path, 0x40) then Com_sprintf(path, maxSize, "%s%s", oldPath, extension). tests/differential/test_q_shared.py covers a 70-character path.

description: A destsize of 0 writes dest[-1]; a negative one copies all of src and writes before dest. Only an assert guards it, and retail builds compile asserts out.
evidence: Disassembly at 0078E080: dest[destsize - 1] = 0 unconditionally; the copy loop counts destsize down to 0.

description: A '?' facing the end of the string steps past the terminator and keeps matching whatever follows in memory.
evidence: Disassembly at 0078E3F8: '?' matches any character, including the terminator, without stopping.

description: Indexes s_clientSamples with talker before its range check (an assert, compiled out of retail builds), so an out-of-range talker reads and then writes (s_clientTalkTime) past the 18-entry arrays.
evidence: Disassembly at 0079DFCE: CMP [EBX*4 + s_clientSamples], 0 before the assert at 0079DFFB; 0079E02D writes s_clientTalkTime[talker]. Where talker comes from (a packet's client number?) isn't checked yet.

description: Saves one entry per mixer with a wave-in line into the 8-entry s_waveInLineInfo with no bound: a ninth such mixer writes past it into the globals that follow.
evidence: Disassembly: the table pointer advances per found line and is never compared with the end; tests/differential/test_win_voice.py runs it with up to 10 mixers.
enhanced: fixed P0001 (the enhanced build never builds the table)

description: The microphone gain (voice_current_scaler) multiplies each captured 16-bit sample and converts back with no clamp, so any gain above 1 makes loud samples wrap around instead of clipping: harsh distortion.
evidence: Pseudocode at 0068BDA0: sample = (short)(int)((float)sample * voice_current_scaler). winvoice_mic_scaler allows up to 2.0.

description: winvoice_mic_scaler ("Microphone scaler value", 0.25-2.0) is registered but nothing in the server copies it into voice_current_scaler, the gain the capture code applies, so the setting does nothing and the gain stays 1.0. To check in the Store client.
evidence: voice_current_scaler (initialised 1.0) is read only in Record_QueueAudioDataForEncoding; no code in CoDMPServer_PC writes it.

description: Driving a vehicle, the stance key presses KB_DOWN (IN_Stance_Down) but its release lets go of KB_VEHICLEMOVEDOWN instead (IN_Stance_Up), so KB_DOWN stays held until some other key bound to it is released. While it is held, every stance change (CL_SetStance, CL_ToggleStance, +gostand, IN_Stance_*, IN_LowerStance/RaiseStance) is ignored, so stance can stick after leaving the vehicle. To check in the Store client and in play.
evidence: Disassembly 004EB5E0 (IN_Stance_Down: playersKb[lc][0xB]) vs 004EB730 (IN_Stance_Up: playersKb[lc][0x29]); tests/differential/test_cl_input.py IN_Stance_Down/Up with eFlags 0x4000.

description: Mouse movement is read from the Windows cursor (GetCursorPos minus last frame's position, then SetCursorPos back to the window centre), not from the device. Windows' pointer settings apply to it ("Enhance pointer precision" acceleration, pointer speed scaling), and the cursor stops at the screen's edges, so in windowed mode a movement larger than the distance from the centre to the edge within one frame is cut short (fullscreen also clamps to the window rectangle, IN_ClampMouseMove). Counts below one pixel of cursor motion are lost.
evidence: IN_MouseMove 00797DC0, IN_ClampMouseMove 00797D50, IN_RecenterMouse 00797C70; tests/differential/test_win_input.py. Every player's mouse input goes through it.

description: CL_MouseMove's AimOutput is a local that only AimAssist_ApplyAutoMelee fills in meleeChargeEnt and meleeChargeDist; AimAssist_UpdateMouseInput skips it when aim assist isn't initialized for the client or the copied weapon state is 0x38-0x3A (low-ready loop, low-ready drop, crawl in), and SetMeleeChargeCmd then copies whatever was on the stack into the usercmd's meleeChargeEnt and meleeChargeDist, which go to the server. The Store build does the same (its inlined copy). What the server does with a stale melee-charge entity is to check.
evidence: AimAssist_UpdateMouseInput 004096C0 (the weapon-state test and the initialized early return), SetMeleeChargeCmd 004EBE80; Store CL_MouseMove 1401930F0 copies [RSP+0x4C]/[RSP+0x4E] unconditionally. tests/differential/test_cl_input.py's Store case reaches it (the harness fills the stack with a fixed pattern so both runs read the same bytes). Reached in normal play whenever the weapon is lowered or the player crawls.

description: CL_MouseMove takes the frame's mouse movement (CL_GetMouseMovement clears it) before returning when frame_msec is 0, so a frame that rounds to 0 ms drops whatever the mouse did in it. frame_msec is whole milliseconds, so at 1000 FPS and above some frames are 0 ms and their movement is lost; the faster the frame rate, the more is lost.
evidence: src/client/cl_input.cpp CL_MouseMove: CL_GetMouseMovement, then `if (!frame_msec) return`; tests/enhanced/test_mouse.py check_zero_ms_frame_keeps_the_movement shows the original taking the movement in a 0 ms frame. Both builds; com_maxfps allows 1000.

description: The view's yaw (clientActive_t.viewangles.y) is never wrapped: turning the same way keeps adding to it, and a float's step grows with its size (0.0005 degrees at 4096, 0.008 at 131072), so after many turns in one direction small mouse movements are rounded to that step. A mouse count is about 0.01 degrees at common settings.
evidence: src/client/cl_input.cpp CL_MouseMove subtracts the yaw from viewangles.y with no wrap; nothing else in cl_input.cpp wraps it (CL_CreateCmd only limits the pitch). tests/enhanced/test_mouse.py check_yaw_stays_in_range.

description: Key events carry the Windows message's time (MSG.time, GetTickCount's milliseconds since the PC booted), but the buttons measure against com_frameTime (timeGetTime() minus its value when the game started). IN_KeyDown stores the boot-clock time as the button's downtime, so the first CL_KeyState after a press computes com_frameTime - downtime, about minus the PC's uptime, and counts the press frame as 0; it then resets downtime to com_frameTime, so IN_KeyUp adds (boot-clock release time - game-clock downtime), about the uptime, and the release frame counts in full. A held movement key starts up to a frame late and always runs to the end of its release frame. A press and release within one frame use the same clock and come out right. After 24.8 days of uptime the difference changes sign and the effects swap.
evidence: Win_GetEvent sets g_wv.sysMsgTime (1421E4548) from MSG.time at 14049BADB; MainWndProc passes it to Sys_QueEvent (14049B890) for SE_KEY and SE_CHAR (1404A03C5, 1404A0451 on); Com_EventLoop passes evTime to CL_KeyEvent, which formats it into the +button command (server 00500DD0); com_frameTime (141F04894) is timeGetTime() - 1421E448C (1403A2A1E, 1403A55F3). Reachable on every key press.

description: Even on one clock, MSG.time only advances with Windows' timer tick (about 15.6 ms), and key messages are read once a frame, so a key's press and release times are only known to about 16 ms. At high frame rates a short tap or the start and end of a held movement key are placed up to a frame or more away from when they happened.
evidence: MSG.time is GetTickCount's clock; Win_GetEvent pumps messages once per Com_EventLoop

description: The adapter r_adapter picks (dx.adapterIndex) is enumerated with EnumAdapters1 and then never used: both D3D11CreateDeviceAndSwapChain and NVAPI's are called with a null adapter, so the device is always made on the default adapter, and the enumerated IDXGIAdapter1 is leaked (its pointer is overwritten by GetParent's)
evidence: src/gfx_d3d/r_init.cpp R_CreateDeviceInternal; Store 14071FF8D (EnumAdapters1 into [RBP-0x80]), 14072002D / 140720192 (first argument 0), 1407201C9 (GetParent into [RBP-0x80])

description: D3D11CreateDeviceAndSwapChain's result is not checked (only NVAPI's is): when it fails, dx.device stays null and the QueryInterface right after it faults instead of reporting the failure. The same function also calls GetFullscreenState on dx.swapChain without checking it, and uses GetContainingOutput's output without checking that call
evidence: src/gfx_d3d/r_init.cpp R_CreateDeviceInternal; Store 140720192 (result discarded), 1407201B5, 1407202D3, 14072022C; tests/differential/test_r_init.py keeps the failing creations out (the original faults on them)

description: On the NVIDIA path NvAPI_Stereo_IsActivated's output is read back without checking the call: when it fails, dx.nvStereoActivated comes from whatever byte sits in the unused second parameter's slot (the caller leaves RDX unset)
evidence: src/gfx_d3d/r_init.cpp R_CreateDeviceInternal; Store 140720066-14072006F; tests/differential/test_r_init.py (stereo_writes = 0)

description: The render thread never blocks: each pass polls its events with zero-timeout waits and, with nothing to do, calls Sleep(0) and polls again. Between frames it spins on a whole core (and Sleep(0) only yields to threads of equal priority), taking CPU time from the main and worker threads that build the next frame. It should wait on its events (WaitForMultipleObjects), with the buffer resize signalled by an event rather than the dx.doResizeBuffers flag it polls
evidence: src/gfx_d3d/rb_backend.cpp RB_RenderThread; Store 140736D60-140737072 (WaitForSingleObject(..., 0) x3, Sleep(0) at 140737074); tests/differential/test_rb_backend.py

description: The swap chain's buffers are resized with the flags fixed at DXGI_SWAP_CHAIN_FLAG_ALLOW_MODE_SWITCH instead of the swap chain's own, and ResizeBuffers' result is ignored. A swap chain created with other flags (the flip model's ALLOW_TEARING or FRAME_LATENCY_WAITABLE_OBJECT, which cannot be changed by ResizeBuffers) fails to resize and keeps drawing at the old size
evidence: src/gfx_d3d/rb_backend.cpp RB_ResizeBuffers (inlined in RB_RenderThread); Store 14073703E (flags 2), 14073704A (result discarded)
